{{nihongo|'''Homi Shrine'''|穂見神社 (南アルプス市)}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takao}}, {{ill|Minami-Alps, Yamanashi|Q824000|qid=Q824000}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|Q132720|qid=Q132720}}. {{nihongo|'''Homi Shrine'''|穂見神社 (南アルプス市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kai Province]].
== Overview ==
'''Homi Shrine''' stands in Takao, a mountain settlement on the northeastern slope of {{ill|Mount Kushigata|Q11544680|qid=Q11544680|lt=Mount Kushigata}}, in {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|Q132720|qid=Q132720}}{{ill|Minami-Alps, Yamanashi|Q824000|qid=Q824000}}. It is commonly called '''Takaozan Homi Shrine''', "Takao-san," or "Yama no Takao"<ref>[http://www.yamanashi-jinjacho.or.jp/intro/list/detail_no/5098 Yamanashi Shrine Office] and [http://www.pref.yamanashi.jp/shigaku/documents/240401syukyohojinmeibo.pdf Religious corporations in Yamanashi (official Yamanashi Prefecture site)]</ref>. Its former rank is {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. The '{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}' lists a "Homi Shrine" among Kai Province {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}; besides this shrine, several other shrines named Homi Shrine exist in Yamanashi (including {{ill|Nirasaki, Yamanashi|Q290326|qid=Q290326}} and {{ill|Shōwa, Yamanashi|Q1204276|qid=Q1204276}}), and this shrine is considered one possible identification of that Engishiki shrine.

It is also widely known in and outside the prefecture as a shrine for business prosperity, conferral of capital, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=sericulture}}. Takao-kō confraternities exist as far away as Tokyo and Nagano, and worshippers visit from afar. In the past, the {{ill|Yamanashi Kōtsū tram line|Q11469607|qid=Q11469607}} ("Boro-den") had {{ill|Sōkomachi Station|Q11386643|qid=Q11386643}} in former Kushigata Town and was used by pilgrims.

== Architecture ==
The '''{{ill|Honden|Q2044994|qid=Q2044994}}''' is a sangen-sha nagare-zukuri building: 5.10 m beam length, 3.20 m depth, ridge height 9.30 m, floor area 25.91 m². It stands on a rubble-stone platform with copper-plate roofing. The current honden is an early {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} robust structure retaining {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Momoyama-period}} style, rebuilt in {{ill|Kanbun (era)|es|Kanbun|fa|کانبون (دوره)|fr|Ère Kanbun|id|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|ko|간분|ru|Камбун (нэнго)|simple|Kanbun (era)|sr|Канбун (ера)|sv|Kanbun|tr|Kanbun (dönem)|zh|寬文|qid=Q1146228}} 5 ({{ill|1665|Q7582|qid=Q7582}}). In recent years, roof copper sheets were re-laid. It was designated a prefectural tangible cultural property in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 40 ({{ill|1965|Q2650|qid=Q2650}}).

The '''{{ill|Kagura-den|Q94498|qid=Q94498}}''' in the precinct was built in {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 24 ({{ill|1891|Q7837|qid=Q7837}}), one-bay by one-bay, four-sided {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|de|Irimoya|es|Tejado de gabletes de Asia oriental|fr|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造|ko|팔작지붕|ru|Иримоя-дзукури|uk|Напіввальмовий дах|zh|歇山顶|qid=Q855025}}, with {{ill|Karahafu|Q977293|qid=Q977293}} on the eaves. Carvings of the {{ill|Four Symbols|Q1073260|qid=Q1073260}} are placed on all four sides, giving it an ornate appearance.

Also dedicated in the precinct is the "Horse of Takao," said to be the work of Edo-period carver Hidari Jingorō.

== Enshrined deity ==
The enshrined deity is {{ill|Ukemochi|Q2280323|qid=Q2280323}}.

== Annual festival ==
The '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Daidai Kagura}}''' held every year on November 22 is designated an intangible folk cultural property of Minami-Alps City and draws many visitors.

== Cultural properties ==
== Yamanashi Prefecture designated tangible cultural properties ==
* Homi Shrine honden (with ridge tags)
* Homi Shrine bronze kakebotoke ("male deity mirror image," goshōtai)
: A {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}} {{ill|Mirror image|Q2703478|qid=Q2703478}}<ref name="#1">'Treasures of Yamanashi,' p.129</ref>, cast in bronze<ref name="#1"/>. Mirror diameter 26.4 cm, rim thickness 0.5 cm<ref name="#1"/>. Inscriptions on both sides of the mirror face include a date of {{ill|Tenpuku|Q1194452|qid=Q1194452|lt=Tenpuku}} 1 ({{ill|1233|Q5421|qid=Q5421}})<ref name="#1"/>. A slightly curved circular mirror face bears an incised seated image of a male deity<ref name="#1"/>. Two cast lugs with circular perforations appear at the top. The inscription includes "Santai Ōji," interpreted as referring to "Daifuku Ōji, Daijumyō Ōji, Daichitoku Ōji" in vol.67 "Misaki Myōjin, Takao Village" of '{{ill|Kaikokushi|Q11577871|qid=Q11577871}}'<ref name="#1"/>. The back also bears the name "Daikanjin Renkōbō Benkei"<ref name="#1"/>.

== Minami-Alps City designated cultural properties ==
* Takao Homi Shrine Kaguraden (tangible cultural property)
* Takao Homi Shrine Daidai Kagura (intangible folk cultural property)
* Great cedar of Takao Homi Shrine (natural monument)
